title: Prevalence and Clinical Significance of Gastric-Type Mucosal Lesions in Non-Ampullary Duodenal Epithelial Tumors Based on Mucin Phenotype

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Prevalence and Clinical Significance of Gastric-Type Mucosal Lesions in Non-Ampullary Duodenal Epithelial Tumors Based on Mucin Phenotype》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · deo270443-sec-0060-p2】Several gastric‐type mucosal lesions (G‐MLs), including gastric foveolar metaplasia, gastric heterotopia, and Brunner's gland hyperplasia, may be observed in the duodenum [3]. In the present study, these lesions were collectively referred to as G‐MLs because they share gastric‐type epithelial features. Matsubara et al. [4] reported activating mutations in GNAS and KRAS in gastric foveolar metaplasia, gastric heterotopia, and duodenal adenocarcinoma. However, the clinical association between G‐MLs and G‐NADETs has not been adequately investigated.

【Introduction · deo270443-sec-0060-p4】We hypothesized that the prevalence of concomitant G‐MLs differs according to the mucin phenotype of NADETs. Therefore, we aimed to assess the prevalence of G‐MLs in patients with NADETs and evaluate their association with the mucin phenotype of NADETs, as well as other clinicopathological factors, including EGMA, Helicobacter pylori infection status, smoking status, alcohol consumption habit, body mass index (BMI), and proton pump inhibitor (PPI) or potassium‐competitive acid blocker (PCAB) use.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Prevalence and Clinical Significance of Gastric-Type Mucosal Lesions in Non-Ampullary Duodenal Epithelial Tumors Based on Mucin Phenotype》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Study Design and Patient Selection · deo270443-sec-0080-p1】This retrospective cross‐sectional study was conducted at Shizuoka General Hospital. Consecutive Japanese patients with NADETs who underwent endoscopic or surgical resection between January 2015 and August 2021 were retrospectively identified.

【Study Design and Patient Selection · deo270443-sec-0080-p2】Of 174 patients with 178 NADET lesions registered during the study period, patients were excluded because of inadequate visualization of the stomach and duodenum (n = 4), biopsy‐only diagnosis (n = 15), familial adenomatous polyposis (n = 5), history of upper gastrointestinal surgery (n = 7), unknown H. pylori infection status (n = 8), or unclassifiable mucin phenotype based on immunohistochemistry (n = 5). For patients with synchronous multiple NADETs, only the largest lesion was included. Finally, 130 patients with 130 lesions were analyzed (Figure 1).

evidence.text: This retrospective cross‐sectional study was conducted at Shizuoka General Hospital. Consecutive Japanese patients with NADETs who underwent endoscopic or surgical resection between January 2015 and August 2021 were retrospectively identified.

Of 174 patients with 178 NADET lesions registered during the study period, patients were excluded because of inadequate visualization of the stomach and duodenum (n = 4), biopsy‐only diagnosis (n = 15), familial adenomatous polyposis (n = 5), history of upper gastrointestinal surgery (n = 7), unknown H. pylori infection status (n = 8), or unclassifiable mucin phenotype based on immunohistochemistry (n = 5). For patients with synchronous multiple NADETs, only the largest lesion was included. Finally, 130 patients with 130 lesions were analyzed (Figure 1).

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Prevalence and Clinical Significance of Gastric-Type Mucosal Lesions in Non-Ampullary Duodenal Epithelial Tumors Based on Mucin Phenotype》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】Concomitant G-MLs were identified in 44 patients (33.8%). Their prevalence was higher in gastric-type tumors (13/16; 81.3%) than in gastric-intestinal-type tumors (10/37; 27.0%) and intestinal-type tumors (21/77; 27.3%). G-MLs were associated with mild endoscopic gastric mucosal atrophy and smoking status and were inversely associated with current Helicobacter pylori infection. In the exploratory fully adjusted model, gastric-type tumors remained positively associated with the presence of G-MLs (adjusted odds ratio, 7.00; 95% confidence interval, 1.98-30.95; p = 0.002).

【Conclusions · abstract-4-1】G-MLs were present in approximately one-third of patients and were most frequent in gastric-type tumors. These findings indicate an association between G-MLs and gastric-type tumors; however, the cross-sectional design does not allow inference of a biological relationship.

【FIGURE 1 · deo270443-fig-0001】FIGURE 1 Patient flowchart. NADET, non‐ampullary duodenal epithelial tumor; G‐NADET, gastric‐type NADET; GI‐NADET, gastric–intestinal‐type NADET; I‐NADET, intestinal‐type NADET.

【FIGURE 2 · deo270443-fig-0002】FIGURE 2 Representative endoscopic, histological, and immunohistochemical findings of a gastric‐type non‐ampullary duodenal epithelial tumor. (a) White‐light endoscopy showing a type 0‐IIc lesion on the side opposite the duodenal papilla. A concomitant gastric‐type mucosal lesion is present proximal to the papilla. (b) Magnifying narrow‐band imaging showing irregularly arranged gastric pit‐like structures of varying sizes within the depressed area. (c) Hematoxylin and eosin‐stained image showing a high‐grade epithelial neoplasm confined to the mucosa, corresponding to category 4.4 according to the revised Vienna classification. (d, e) Immunohistochemical staining positive for MUC5AC and MUC6. (f, g) Immunohistochemical staining negative for MUC2 and CD10.

【FIGURE 3 · deo270443-fig-0003】FIGURE 3 Representative endoscopic and histological findings of a gastric‐type mucosal lesion with gastric foveolar metaplasia. (a) White‐light endoscopic image showing a 3‐mm lesion in the duodenal bulb. (b) Magnifying narrow‐band imaging showing relatively regular gastric pit‐like surface structures. (c) Hematoxylin and eosin‐stained image of the biopsy specimen showing gastric foveolar metaplasia.
